items.title: New grads have to compete with AI for entry
items.summary: A new report reveals that 48% of hiring managers would rather invest in AI tools than hire and train recent college graduates, raising the entry-level hiring bar and putting pressure on business majors to quickly demonstrate practical digital and workplace skills.

items.title: 9 Powerful AI Jobs in Business That Use AI Tools
items.summary: The demand for non-technical AI roles across corporate departments means that business majors must focus on building prompt writing, data interpretation, and workflow automation skills rather than complex software engineering.

items.title: How AI Is Changing Business Careers: The Future of Work
items.summary: As automation absorbs repetitive, data-heavy tasks, the career trajectory of junior business analysts is shifting toward high-value work like interpreting AI-generated insights and driving corporate strategy.

items.title: Healthcare Professionals Transitioning to AI Careers
items.summary: A surging demand for AI-literate clinical staff is pushing healthcare graduates and professionals toward hybrid AI roles, with job growth in medical AI positions projected to increase by 30% through 2028.

items.title: AI-Driven Sector Growth in Public Health Education
items.summary: The intersection of healthcare technology and automation is expanding career opportunities for health education majors, who are increasingly being hired to build and oversee AI-powered training models for patients and providers.

items.title: AI Is Changing Creative Work, but the Arts Aren't Disappearing
items.summary: A recent labor study shows that despite rising anxieties over job displacement, generative AI has not significantly depressed artists' earnings, instead serving primarily as a collaborative tool for early-stage brainstorming and workflow organization.

items.title: What Skills Do Art Studies Graduates Need to Work with AI?
items.summary: Rapid AI integration in digital media and entertainment is driving a 15% projected industry growth, forcing arts graduates to combine their creative visions with technical AI proficiency to adapt to increasingly automated workflows.

items.title: Will AI Replace Creative Jobs? What Students Need to Know
items.summary: Educational leaders emphasize that creative arts programs must now teach students to treat generative AI as a workflow and logistics collaborator rather than a replacement for core human authorship and creative leadership.

items.title: AI Impact on Student Career Choices: Survey Reveals 4 in 10 Rethinking College Majors
items.summary: As students increasingly seek "AI-resistant" careers, higher education enrollment is shifting away from computer science toward programs that blend technical skills with liberal arts and human-centric qualities like empathy and complex problem-solving.

items.title: Career Growth and Employment Projections for Humanities Graduates
items.summary: Driven by diverse workplace environments and complex compliance demands, employers are prioritizing humanities graduates who offer strong global competencies and ethical reasoning skills to navigate emerging AI technologies.

items.title: Key Things to Know About AI, Automation, and the Future of Humanities Degree Careers
items.summary: While AI automation is poised to impact nearly 45% of tasks within traditional humanities occupations, it is simultaneously boosting higher-paying opportunities in interdisciplinary areas like ethical AI development and digital storytelling.

items.title: Key Things to Know About AI, Automation, and the Future of Sociology Degree Careers
items.summary: Nearly 70% of social science roles now require proficiency in AI-assisted data analysis, which has driven a 12% salary premium for sociologists who can successfully combine technical AI knowledge with traditional sociological expertise.

items.title: Which majors AI is actually killing, and which ones it isn't
items.source: Substack (Analyzing Gallup & National Student Clearinghouse Data)
items.summary: Fearing automated displacement in traditional tech fields, college students are pivoting their academic plans, with 26% of those switching majors electing to move into social sciences to focus on careers requiring high levels of human-centric interaction and physical presence.

items.title: Impact of AI on Early
items.source: National Association of Colleges and Employers (NACE)
items.summary: Over half of surveyed employers are actively discussing how AI can substitute for tasks traditionally assigned to entry-level professionals, heightening career concerns for newly graduating social science majors and urging a shift toward human-AI collaboration skills.

items.title: How AI Is Reshaping the Job Market in 2026: Growing, Shrinking & Transforming Roles
items.summary: AI is transforming STEM careers by driving massive demand for "AI application engineers" who deploy existing machine learning models into practical business workflows, rather than traditional research roles that build models from scratch.

items.title: Impact of AI on Early
items.source: National Association of Colleges and Employers (NACE)
items.summary: Employers are shifting their expectations for recent graduates, increasingly requiring entry-level STEM workers to possess strategic problem-solving and adaptability skills to direct, evaluate, and manage AI-generated work products.

items.title: What it’s like to enter the job market in the middle of an AI revolution
items.summary: Although entry-level job postings in tech-related fields have dipped, labor market experts point out that AI has not yet actively replaced entry-level STEM roles, though roughly 35% of these positions now require some form of AI proficiency.

items.title: Why AI is ‘resurrecting’ the liberal arts for the Class of 2026
items.summary: As generative AI automates technical execution and basic tasks, employers are placing a premium on the "liberal arts brain" to provide ethical oversight, strategic intent, and critical thinking.

items.title: Why the liberal arts can help young Americans prepare for the era of AI
items.summary: Industry and recruiting experts report that because AI can easily handle raw coding and technical execution, employers are increasingly seeking graduates with strong emotional intelligence (EQ), creative lateral thinking, and adaptability.

items.title: Key Things to Know About AI, Automation, and the Future of Humanities Degree Careers
items.summary: While automated tools are reshaping entry-level media and content creation roles, they are simultaneously driving up salaries and demand for interdisciplinary humanities graduates who can provide high-level analysis and digital storytelling.

items.title: Report Highlights Changing Views on Skilled Trades
items.summary: A newly released survey shows that AI's disruption of white-collar security is pushing 76% of Gen Z to seek careers that are difficult to automate, prompting a major shift in interest toward highly secure and lucrative trade careers.

items.title: AI Shifts Labor Demand: Skilled Trades Gain as White-Collar Hiring Slows
items.summary: Major corporations like Ford and AT&T are ramping up recruitment for hands-on trade roles like electricians, technicians, and mechanics as AI reduces entry-level hiring opportunities for college-educated white-collar workers.

items.title: How AI Is Changing Skilled Trades in 2026 (Your Job Is Safer Than You Think)
items.summary: While AI threatens screen-based roles, the technology is actually driving rapid job growth for tradespeople because building and maintaining the massive physical infrastructure for data centers requires on-site electricians, HVAC technicians, and pipefitters.
